## Style notes (derived from the placeholders above)

### Opening

- **Open by challenging an assumption**, not by soft-setting the scene
- Example: "Most readers assume X. That assumption is wrong because..."
- Example: "The first thing to check is not what most guides recommend."
- ❌ Avoid soft openings ("In today's world...", "Have you ever wondered...")
- ❌ Avoid defining the topic before showing there's a problem with it

### Body

- Each H2 answers one specific question a reader would have
- Each H2 opens with a 1-sentence claim, then backs it up with evidence
- Use **bold** for the central term of each paragraph on first use
- Inline links to authoritative sources (≥ 1 per H2)
- Include a "Why this matters" beat at the end of long H2s

### Closing

- Recap 3-5 key takeaways (no more)
- End with a single, specific next action
- ❌ Avoid vague calls-to-action ("Learn more", "Contact us")
- ✅ "If your use case matches X, see [our checklist](https://...)"

### Headlines

- Use Title Case consistently
- Include the primary keyword
- Don't promise what the article can't deliver
- 50-60 characters ideal (search-friendly)
